idiom_name: Express app.use middleware stack (app object as single entry point)
implementation_notes: Node's http.createServer takes one request listener, so the front controller is whatever function you pass there; Express makes the structure explicit: one app object, an ordered middleware stack registered with app.use and a router that dispatches to route handlers, with four-argument error middleware as the single error-mapping stage. What replaces the classic structure: the middleware array plus the router replaces FrontController, dispatcher and helper objects, and req/res carry the request context. File-convention platforms apply the same idea outside Express - a Next.js proxy.js file exports one function that runs before every route.
pitfalls: Forgetting next() hangs the request, and calling next() after res.send() dispatches twice and throws ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT.
An async middleware that rejects without calling next(err) bypasses the error-handling chain and surfaces as an unhandled rejection.
Order matters: a JSON body parser registered after the routes leaves handlers with an empty req.body, and error middleware must be registered last and declare exactly four parameters.
Route pattern syntax changed between Express 4 and 5, so a copied dispatch table (wildcards, optional segments) can silently stop matching.
